steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Nuclear family: two generations (parents and children) living together. Murdock argued the nuclear family is universal and performs four essential functions: sexual, reproductive, economic and educational. Parsons called it the 'isolated nuclear family' - geographically and socially mobile for modern industrial society. | Key Fact: Extended family: three or more generations living together or nearby. Vertical extended: grandparents, parents, children. Horizontal extended: aunts, uncles, cousins. Common in pre-industrial and many non-Western societies; declining in the UK due to geographical mobility. | Key Fact: Reconstituted/step families: formed when adults with children from previous relationships form new partnerships. About 10% of UK families. Challenges: divided loyalties,
